findings.text: follow-on: test_audit_finding_classes_are_emitted asserts the class is a member of AUDIT_FINDING_CLASSES, which ReviewCheck's model_validator already enforces at load, so the assertion cannot fail for any check that loaded and validates nothing about the classes audits.py actually emits; "duplicate_component" is not a finding_type any audit emits (it is AuditReport.duplicate_components) and no test would notice.

follow-on: the checkpoint reports the name axis as 28 checks (grammar 7, semantic 10, convention 8, completeness 3) and docs as 26 (documentation_quality 13, completeness 7); the taxonomy actually holds 32 name-axis checks and 24 docs-axis checks, so the reporting understates the name axis by four.

follow-on: the gate log's first line is the pytest banner rather than a header naming the revision, tree and command it ran at, so a later reader cannot confirm from the log alone which revision produced the nine passes.
